title: The Name my support
hookLine: the true Name is my support and satisfies every hunger (Anand, opening pauris)

lines: THE FRIDGE, THE SCROLL, THE PHONE.
cards: Ever eaten a whole meal and still felt hungry? Not stomach hungry. The other kind.
You finish dinner and find yourself opening the fridge again, or scrolling for something to buy, or reaching for a phone with nothing new on it.
There's a hunger food doesn't touch, and people feed it all day with whatever's nearest, and it never quite fills.
The fourth pauri of Anand Sahib names something it says fills that hunger, all of it, with a word that also means what a building stands on.

teach.b: The pauri begins and ends with one line: saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro. The true Name is my support. Aadhaar means support, foundation, the base a thing rests on; the same word names India's national identity number today.
In the pauri it's the ground under your feet. Then, in paraphrase: it has taken away all my hunger. It brought peace and calm to live in my mind, and fulfilled all my longings.
I am forever a sacrifice to the Guru, who gives such greatness. Says Nanak, listen, saints: love the Word. Three things to notice.

teach.h: THE NAME TAKES AWAY ALL HUNGER.
teach.b: Bhukh is the plain everyday word, the hunger before lunch, and the pauri says the Name takes away all of it: a bold claim, made from experience, not as theory. Second, the order.

teach.h: THEN PEACE MOVES INTO THE MIND.
teach.b: Support first, then hunger gone, then peace comes to live in the mind. Peace isn't chased; it moves in once the foundation is there.
Third, kurbaan, sacrifice: to give yourself wholly, the word people use when they'd do anything for someone.
The joy of the first three pauris turns here into gratitude so full it wants to give itself away.
And the pauri doesn't tell you to stop eating or stop wanting. It describes what happens when the deepest hunger is met: the smaller hungers lose their power. You're fed underneath.

how: Many Sikhs recite this fourth pauri as part of the short Anand Sahib at the close of services, and many remember the Name, saying Waheguru or a short prayer, before eating.

o: a fast kept to quiet the body's hunger
a gift given to the Guru in thanks
support, the foundation a life rests on

s: pauri four tells people to stop eating
it says the Name meets the deepest hunger, so the smaller hungers lose their power.
the pauri begins and ends with the same line
saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro: the true Name is my support.
in the pauri, peace has to be chased
once the foundation is there, peace comes to live in the mind.

games.q: you've eaten and still feel hungry in a way food can't fix. what does pauri four say meets that hunger?
o: the true Name, my support: it takes away all hunger.
games.why: saach naam adhaar meraa jin bhukhaa sabh gavaaeeaa: the true Name is my support, which has taken away all my hunger.

practice: If there's something to eat nearby, a piece of fruit or a sip of tea, take one bite now, or keep this for your next meal. Taste it fully, chew slowly, and notice the moment your body says, that's good.
If you pray, you can say Waheguru first, the way many Sikhs remember the Name before eating; if not, just let the bite be enough.

wordCard.voice: Aadhaar, support or foundation. Saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro: the true Name is my foundation, and it takes away all hunger, so peace can come and live in the mind.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: aadhaar, support or foundation; in pauri four, the true Name is my support.

carryVoice: Your line: my support. A foundation holds up the whole house without being seen. That's day three hundred eighty-five.
